overview: Yemen is a country at the southern end of the Arabian Peninsula. Its capital, Sana'a, is an ancient city famous for its tall mud-brick tower houses. North and South Yemen united in 1990. Since 2014 Yemen has been torn by civil war, which has caused one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

geography.text: Yemen has coastal plains along the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, and high mountains in the west that get enough rain for farming. The east is mostly desert. The island of Socotra, in the Arabian Sea, is famous for strange plants found nowhere else, such as the dragon's blood tree.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Very hot on the coasts, milder in the high mountains.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Socotra island has dragon's blood trees and many unique species.

history.text: Yemen was home to ancient kingdoms such as Saba, linked in legend to the Queen of Sheba, which grew rich trading frankincense and myrrh. In the 1900s the north became independent from the Ottomans, while the south around Aden was a British colony. North and South Yemen united in 1990. A civil war that began in 2014 has caused one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

events.title: Marib Dam
events.text: The kingdom of Saba builds a great dam at Marib.

events.title: North independent
events.text: North Yemen becomes independent as the Ottoman Empire collapses.

events.title: South independent
events.text: Britain leaves Aden and South Yemen becomes independent.

events.title: Civil war
events.text: Houthi forces take Sana'a; a Saudi-led coalition intervenes in 2015.

government.text: Yemen has been divided by civil war since 2014. The internationally recognised government, led by a Presidential Leadership Council, controls the south and east, while the Houthi movement controls the capital, Sana'a, and much of the north. A Saudi-led coalition has fought the Houthis since 2015.

economy.text: Yemen is the poorest country in the Arab world. The war has caused one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with millions needing food aid. Before the war, oil was its main export.

culture.text: Yemen has a rich history from the ancient kingdom of Saba to the mud-brick skyscrapers of Shibam, called the 'Manhattan of the desert'. Mocha, a Yemeni port, gave its name to a type of coffee, which was first drunk in Yemen.

items.title: Shibam
items.text: Mud-brick tower houses up to 30 metres tall.

items.title: Mocha
items.text: The port from which coffee spread to the world.

items.title: Socotra
items.text: An island with strange 'dragon's blood' trees.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Saltah, a spicy stew, is the national dish.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Song of Sana'a, a poetic music tradition, listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Coffee was first brewed in Yemen.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Yemen's young players won the West Asian under-15 championship, a rare source of national celebration during the war.

items.title: Football
items.text: Yemen's youth teams have won regional titles during the war.

didYouKnow: Coffee drinking as we know it began in Yemen in the 1400s.
Socotra's 'dragon's blood' trees are found nowhere else on Earth.

keyPeople.name: Tawakkol Karman
keyPeople.text: Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2011.

keyPeople.name: Queen Arwa
keyPeople.text: Ruled Yemen for decades in the 1000s and 1100s.
